# 1. Organise and clean the data

## 1.1 Subset the data into the specific dataset allocated

*A description of the data set provided, its contents and which subset you should select is documented in the assessment brief at CS5801-Assessment Brief 2026-27.pdf. The metadata for the health club data set (column definitions, units and expected values) is provided with the brief.*

*Use R code to correctly select the subset of data allocated.*

```{r}
# Only change the value for SID
# Assign your student id into the variable SID, for example:
SID <- 2605197
SIDoffset <- (SID %% 50) + 1    # Your SID mod 50 + 1

load("health_club.Rda")
# Now subset the health club data set
# Pick every 50th observation starting from your offset
# Put into your data frame named mydf (you can rename it)
mydf <- df[seq(from=SIDoffset,to=nrow(df),by=50),]
```


# 1. Data quality

## 1.A First look at every column
```{r}
str(mydf)        # column types: is join_date a date? are categories text?
summary(mydf)    # min/max of numeric columns, to compare with the metadata ranges
```

## 1.B Categorical columns: are all values valid?
```{r}
# Valid values come from the metadata in the assessment brief
table(mydf$membership_type)   # should only be Basic, Standard, Premium, Student
table(mydf$joined_via)        # should only be Online, Walk-in, Referral, Corporate
table(mydf$membership_status) # active, active_deal, suspended
table(mydf$cancelled)         # Yes, No
```

## 1.C Rows that break the metadata rules
```{r}
valid_types <- c("Basic", "Standard", "Premium", "Student")
# Misspelt membership_type
mydf[!(mydf$membership_type %in% valid_types), ]

# rating must be 1 to 10
mydf[mydf$rating < 1 | mydf$rating > 10, ]

# join_date must be 2016-01-01 to 2026-09-30
mydf$join_date <- as.Date(mydf$join_date)
mydf[mydf$join_date < as.Date("2016-01-01") | mydf$join_date > as.Date("2026-09-30"), ]

# other ranges from the metadata
sum(mydf$distance < 0.1 | mydf$distance > 40)
sum(mydf$monthly_spend == 0)     # zero spend: possible but worth checking
anyNA(mydf)                      # any missing values?
sum(duplicated(mydf))            # any duplicate rows?
```

## 1.D Does membership_status give away cancelled?
```{r}
table(mydf$membership_status, mydf$cancelled)
```
